12	
13	## Goal
14	Add an easy-to-access text search (with optional RegExp mode and agent-built expressions) over cards, history and other special folders, with grouped results and navigation to the matching card or file, integrated into the borderless window's drag bar area.
15	
16	## Current state
17	There is no search feature: no search service or module, no search UI, no RegExp handling and no agent-built expression flow. The initial description assumed history is "not loaded", but that is no longer true — the data the search needs is already in memory.
18	
19	The parsed project data is available through `useProjectState()`, which returns the `DataService` state including a `ProjectSnapshot` with `activeCards`, `backgroundCards` and `workingFolder`. `markdownParsingService.splitCards` already splits files into active vs background using `isRootWorkingFolderFile` (root markdown files under the working folder are active; everything in subfolders is background), and produces `ProjectCard` objects with `content` (body only), a parsed `header` (`CardHeader`: id, title, status, owner, affects, policy, etc.), `isActive` and `path`. A search module can consume this snapshot directly; frontmatter parsing already lives in `markdown_parsing_service.ts` and must not be duplicated. Background results are not currently grouped by their first subfolder anywhere.
20	
21	The top shell is `MainToolbar` (MUI `AppBar`/`Toolbar`) rendered by `MainWindow`; it holds the "MD²" title, a config `IconButton` and a `toolbarAction` slot (currently `<ThemeControls />` from `app.tsx`). There is no search input in the toolbar. The desktop window is borderless via Electron `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` with a `titleBarOverlay` in `desktop/main.js`; there is no manual CSS drag region (`-webkit-app-region`) anywhere in the React shell, so a custom drag bar and its non-draggable input/button zones do not yet exist.
22	
23	Navigation into a card/file is local to `ProjectWorkspace`, which owns `viewMode` (`'cards' | 'text'`). `handleOpenInFileMode(path)` sets a `requestedPath` + `requestedNonce` and switches to text view; `TextView` opens that path as a tab via `useOpenTabs` and can browse background files through its file tree. There is no shared/global "navigate to card or file, keeping current view" API — selecting a background result without changing view mode is not currently supported. Routing exists via `app_navigation` (`navigateTo` / `useAppLocation`, with a `/config` route), but nothing search-related uses it.
24	
25	There is no agent infrastructure wired up: `App` passes `agents={[]}` to `MainWindow`, so agent-built RegExp has no existing execution path to reuse. No tests cover search.
26	
27	## implementation details
28	- Add a search service or pure search module in `app/src/` that searches the loaded `ProjectSnapshot`; keep storage-specific file loading in the existing GitHub/local storage services.
29	- Search active root cards by full body content and header fields by default. Search background cards from subfolders by header fields by default, with an option to include full body content. Use `ProjectCard` data produced by the shared parsing service; the search module must not parse frontmatter itself.
30	- Support plain case-insensitive contains search and an explicit RegExp mode. Invalid expressions must show a clear validation error and keep previous results stable.
31	- Group results with active cards first, then background results grouped by first folder under the working folder, such as `history` or `architecture`.
32	- Each result shows the card/file title, path, match context and whether the match came from header or body.
33	- Selecting a result navigates to the matching card or file in the current workspace view. If the file is a background card, make it selectable without changing the user's current view mode.
34	- Add the search input and controls to the top shell area while preserving drag behavior in the borderless Electron window; text inputs and buttons must remain non-draggable.
35	- Agent-built RegExp generation is a separate action from manual search input and must surface agent failures without changing the current query.
36	- Tests should cover search matching/grouping, RegExp validation, full-body background search toggling, result selection and toolbar drag/non-drag behavior.
37	
38	## acceptance criteria
39	- A user can run a plain text search from the top shell area without breaking window dragging in the desktop app.
40	- Active cards are searched by full content and appear before background/special-folder results.
41	- Background cards from history, architecture and other subfolders are searchable by header fields; enabling full search includes their body content.
42	- RegExp mode returns matches for valid expressions and reports invalid expressions without crashing or clearing the current query.
43	- Results are grouped by active cards and by special folder name, with enough context to identify the match.
44	- Clicking a result opens/selects the matching card or file while keeping the current workspace view.
45	- Agent-built RegExp can populate the query when successful and leaves the existing query unchanged on failure.
46	- Unit and React tests cover the search module, grouped result rendering, result navigation and shell search controls.
47	
48	## see also
49	- `design\architecture\initial description\search.md`
50	- `design\architecture\parsing_service.md`
51

entries.content:
Now I have a complete picture. Let me understand F_200:

- **Feature**: In global search results, highlight the search term in the context text shown for each result.
- **Current state**: `search_results.tsx` renders `match.context` as a plain string in `secondary` — no highlighting of the matched text within the context snippet.
- The `SearchMatch` has `context` (a raw text string with surrounding text) and the `search_project.ts` `buildContext` function returns just text — no position/offset info for the match within the context string.
- There's no component for rendering highlighted text in search results, so I'll need to either pass the match position down to `SearchResults` for highlighting, or restructure `SearchMatch.context` to carry the matched range explicitly. Looking at `buildContext`, it slices a snippet from `text` using a `MatchLocation`, so I can compute where the match falls within that snippet accounting for the ellipsis prefix, and expose that as a `matchRange` on the result.

Alternatively, the simpler route is to re-find the query string within the context at render time inside `SearchResults`, passing along the query and mode (text/regexp) so it can build a matcher per-result without changing the `SearchMatch` type at all -- that feels cleaner for this codebase. I still need to decide whether to use MUI's `mark` element or a custom styled span, and whether `ActionSearchMatch` needs the same treatment.

`SearchPanel` already has `query` and `mode`, so I just need to thread them down to `SearchResults`. For matching, I'll re-run regex or case-insensitive indexOf against the context string at render time, with no changes needed to `SearchMatch` or `search_project.ts`, and style the highlight with the theme's warning color. If the match can't be relocated due to whitespace normalization or regex flags, I'll just fall back to rendering plain text.

Action search matches should get the same highlighting treatment, again without touching the underlying types or service. I'm noting that `buildContext` normalizes whitespace via a regex replace and trim, which could occasionally cause regexp matches spanning whitespace to not re-find cleanly -- worth flagging as an implementation detail. Now I'll write up the feature document concisely but completely.

Now I have the complete picture. Let me write the feature description.

**Current state**:
- Search is fully implemented (F_017 complete). `search_project.ts` produces `SearchMatch` objects with a `context` string (plain text snippet, ±40 chars around the match, whitespace-normalized). `search_results.tsx` renders `context` as a plain secondary string in `ListItemText.secondary` — no visual distinction of the matched portion. Same for `ActionSearchMatch.context`.
- `buildContext` does not preserve the match offset within the returned snippet — it returns a raw string only.
- `SearchPanel` owns `query` and `mode` but doesn't pass them down to `SearchResults`, so I need to thread those through as props and re-locate the match within each context string to highlight it with a `<mark>` element, styled via MUI's sx prop.

I'll apply the same highlighting logic to `renderActionMatch`, and handle the edge case where whitespace normalization in `buildContext` causes the match to not be re-findable — falling back to plain text rather than throwing. No changes needed to the underlying types or search logic files. The acceptance criteria center on visually distinguishing matched text in both search modes while gracefully degrading when a match can't be relocated.
